title: LibWstethEthOracle returns 0 when Chainlink and Uniswap diverge >1% (no documented fallback)

location.code_snippet: if (getPercentDifference(chainlinkPrice, uniswapPrice) < MAX_DIFFERENCE) { wstethEthPrice = (chainlinkPrice + uniswapPrice)/2; ... } // no else -> returns 0 on divergence

description: getWstethEthPrice computes a Chainlink-derived price and a Uniswap V3 TWAP price, then only assigns wstethEthPrice inside `if (getPercentDifference(chainlinkPrice, uniswapPrice) < MAX_DIFFERENCE)` (1%). When the two sources differ by >=1%, the if-block is skipped and the function returns the default 0. The NatSpec (L29-35) documents a richer policy ('minimum of (3) and either the average of (1) and (2) ... or (1)'), but the implemented code has NO else branch and NO fall-through to source (1) or (3): it simply returns 0. A returned 0 propagates as an oracle-failure sentinel (getUsdPrice/getWstethUsdPrice return 0; LibWell.getRatiosAndBeanIndex sets success=false; LibWellMinting.twaDeltaB treats the minting oracle as 'off' and returns deltaB=0; LibDeltaB.calculateDeltaBFromReserves reverts 'USD Oracle call failed').
impact: Any time the Chainlink wstETH:ETH feed and the Uniswap wstETH:ETH TWAP diverge by >=1% (plausible during volatility, a stETH depeg, or sustained Uniswap manipulation pressure), the wstETH oracle returns 0. For the BEAN:WSTETH well this turns the minting/deltaB oracle off (deltaB=0 in sunrise) or reverts convert deltaB pricing (LibDeltaB), pausing wstETH-well minting and conversions until the sources re-converge. Availability/DoS impact on the wstETH well during exactly the market conditions where pricing matters most. Whether this is the intended conservative behavior or a missing fallback cannot be inferred from comments (which describe a different policy); flagged as a behavioral/availability gap.

ite.intent: Produce a manipulation-resistant wstETH:ETH price, falling back across 3 sources per the documented policy.
ite.technique: The if-block guarding the average assignment has no else; on >=1% divergence the function returns the default 0 instead of any fallback source.
ite.evasion: The 1% MAX_DIFFERENCE check looks like a manipulation guard, but the failure mode is silent oracle-off rather than the documented min/fallback.

ice_chain.consumer_action: minting oracle treated as off (deltaB=0) or convert deltaB pricing reverts for the BEAN:WSTETH well
